title: UK monthly GDP + Index of Production + Index of Services, August 2026 (ONS, 07:00 London / 02:00 ET) — one slot, three bulletins
source: EST: three ONS release pages fetched direct 2026-09-10, HTTP 200 each — ons.gov.uk/releases/gdpmonthlyestimateukaugust2026, .../indexofproductionukaugust2026 and .../indexofservicesukaugust2026 — all three reading verbatim 'Release date: 15 October 2026 7:00am' and 'This release is not yet published'. NOTE THE DISTINCTION THE PUBLISHER MAKES: these carry a plain 'Release date', not the 'Provisional release date' that the proposing lane's own Blue Book 2026 page and the Pink Book 2026 page carry — the ONS treats the monthly slot as firm and the October compendium slot as provisional. The next edition in the same series (September 2026 data) reads '12 November 2026 7:00am' on all three pages, a four-week cadence consistent with the monthly series. Filed estimate on two counts only, one fewer than the compendium entries: the confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no slot for a foreign national statistics institute, and this lane does not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep — the date itself is not labelled provisional by anyone
notes: PROPOSED BY THE uk-blue-book-2026-10-30 LANE, 2026-09-10, during that event's never-assessed initial research. Proposed because it is the load-bearing date under that lane's central finding, and the finding is weaker without it on the calendar. The Blue Book compendium's own Release policy section names the mid-October monthly bulletins as the FRESHEST inputs it contains — Blue Book 2025's background notes (fetched direct, HTTP 200) list 'our Index of Production bulletin, published on 16 October 2025' and 'our Index of Services bulletin, published on 16 October 2025'; Blue Book 2024's list the 11 October 2024 pair. So 2026-10-15 is the last moment at which anything inside the 2026-10-30 compendium becomes public, which is what makes 'every input is already published before publication day' a dated claim rather than a rhetorical one. Independently, this is the UK's own most timely activity read and this calendar tracks NO UK monthly GDP release at all — it carries UK CPI, PPI, labour market, public sector finances and quarterly national accounts, but nothing monthly on output — so this entry also closes a coverage gap rather than only serving the proposer. The proposing lane makes NO claim about this release's market impact: no monthly-GDP event study was run, symbols is empty, and the LOW tier is inherited from the ONS family. Estimate widens caution only; nothing date-keyed may act on this.
